title: Query Performance Testing and Regression Analysis
learningObjectives: Distinguish query correctness from query performance.
Measure execution time in a reliable client or benchmark harness.
Use repeatable data and parameters for comparisons.
Record performance measurements with workload context.
Detect regressions without relying on a single timing sample.

understand.concept: Performance testing measures how a query behaves under a defined workload. A reliable comparison controls data, parameters, cache conditions, concurrency and measurement method.
understand.whyItMatters: A query that is fast on a tiny sample may become slow at production scale, and one timing sample can be distorted by caching or background work.
understand.analogy: A runner's time is meaningful only when the distance, conditions and timing method are consistent.
understand.analogyLimit: SQL itself does not provide a portable, reliable wall-clock benchmark for every engine. The client or benchmark harness should measure elapsed time and record environment details.

explain.narrative:
## Benchmark discipline
Define the query, parameters, data volume, expected result, concurrency level and measurement method. Warm-up runs, repeated measurements and percentile summaries are more useful than a single fastest run.

## Correctness before speed
Compare the result sets before comparing timings. A faster query that drops rows, changes NULL handling or alters aggregation is not a valid optimization.

## Record context
Store query version, test dataset, engine/version, run timestamp, row count and measured duration. The duration should come from a monotonic client-side timer or engine-specific profiling tool, not from an arbitrary SQL expression.

## Regression review
Compare medians or percentiles over repeated runs and investigate material regressions. Re-check plans after schema or statistics changes and avoid asserting exact elapsed milliseconds in a lesson's expected SQL output.

### Timer choice
Use a monotonic high-resolution timer supplied by the browser or runtime when measuring elapsed duration. Wall-clock time can jump because of clock synchronization or manual adjustment. Keep warm-up samples separate, repeat the workload and report a distribution such as median and p95.

examples.title: Create a table for repeatable benchmark data
examples.code: CREATE TABLE perf22_benchmark_rows (row_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, category TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: Creates a small benchmark fixture. Performance conclusions from this fixture are illustrative only; production tuning needs representative data size and distribution.

examples.title: Generate 200 deterministic benchmark rows
examples.code: WITH RECURSIVE seq(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM seq WHERE n < 200) INSERT INTO perf22_benchmark_rows SELECT n, CASE WHEN n % 5 = 0 THEN 'rare' ELSE 'common' END, n * 10 FROM seq;
examples.explanation: Creates 40 rare and 160 common rows. Deterministic data allows the same query to be compared across test runs.

examples.title: Create a benchmark index
examples.explanation: Adds an index for category filtering. Measure whether it helps the tested query rather than assuming it is always beneficial.

examples.title: Record client-measured query runs
examples.code: CREATE TABLE perf22_query_runs (run_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, query_version TEXT NOT NULL, engine_version TEXT NOT NULL, dataset_label TEXT NOT NULL, elapsed_ms REAL NOT NULL CHECK (elapsed_ms >= 0), measured_at TEXT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO perf22_query_runs VALUES (1, 'v1', 'SQLite 3.46.1', '200-row-fixture', 2.4, '2026-11-22T10:00:00Z'), (2, 'v1', 'SQLite 3.46.1', '200-row-fixture', 2.1, '2026-11-22T10:01:00Z'), (3, 'v2', 'SQLite 3.46.1', '200-row-fixture', 1.8, '2026-11-22T10:02:00Z'), (4, 'v2', 'SQLite 3.46.1', '200-row-fixture', 1.9, '2026-11-22T10:03:00Z');
examples.explanation: Stores example timing observations produced by a client-side benchmark harness. The values are synthetic teaching data; SQL did not measure its own elapsed time. A real harness should use a monotonic high-resolution timer, run warm-up and repeated samples, and record the exact parameters and environment. Do not use wall-clock timestamps as elapsed-time measurements.

examples.title: Compare average recorded durations by query version
examples.code: SELECT query_version, ROUND(AVG(elapsed_ms), 2) AS average_ms FROM perf22_query_runs GROUP BY query_version ORDER BY query_version;
examples.explanation: Calculates the average of the stored measurements: v1 averages 2.25 ms and v2 averages 1.85 ms. A real decision should use more repetitions, percentiles, result-equivalence checks and the same test conditions.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and calculate the two averages. Explain why the numbers are labelled synthetic and what a real benchmark must control before claiming an improvement.
practise.independentTask: Create a benchmark plan for a slow report. Include at least 10 repeated runs, a warm-up policy, fixed parameters, result comparison, engine version, median/p95 reporting and a rollback threshold.
hints: Correctness checks come before timing comparisons.
Use repeatable data and identical parameters.
Measure elapsed time in the client or benchmark harness.
Use repeated samples and percentiles, not one run.
Record engine version, dataset and query version.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before comparing query speed?
options: That the queries return equivalent results
That the query strings have equal length
That one query has more joins
questions.answer: That the queries return equivalent results
questions.explanation: Performance is not an improvement if the result changes incorrectly.

questions.prompt: Where should portable elapsed-time measurement usually occur?
options: In a client or benchmark harness using a reliable timer
questions.answer: In a client or benchmark harness using a reliable timer
questions.explanation: SQL timing facilities differ by engine; a client harness provides controlled measurement.

options: To reduce the influence of noise and cache variation
questions.answer: To reduce the influence of noise and cache variation
questions.explanation: Repeated runs support more robust comparisons.

questions.prompt: Which summary is often more useful than the single fastest run?
options: The row count of the query text
questions.explanation: Percentiles help describe typical and tail latency.

questions.prompt: What context should a benchmark record?
options: Engine version, dataset, query version and parameters
questions.answer: Engine version, dataset, query version and parameters
questions.explanation: Context makes measurements reproducible and interpretable.
